items.headline: Frontier Model Review Board executive order — post-briefing procedural phase
items.diff_narrative: Friday was the S-407 classified threshold briefing itself; Saturday moves into the post-briefing record. Friday's classified-annex follow-up question set, which the unclassified summary memo said would go to the witnesses, is now formally transmitted to the eight-witness slate, with the ten-business-day response clock running from the Friday transmittal. The new framing is procedural: a Just Security Saturday analysis reads the briefing's no-objection finding on the state attorney-general consultation pathway and the AISI 120-day reciprocity placement window as having removed the principal cited signing-window blocker, while OSTP holds the no-signing-before-May-22 line unchanged. The House parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft text continues circulating for markup scheduling.

items.headline: Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter — Qatar formalizes
items.diff_narrative: Friday stepped the count from thirteen to fourteen jurisdictions with Saudi Arabia's formal entry and Qatar signalling adjacent-track interest. Saturday converts Qatar's Friday adjacent-track interest note into a formal exploratory-observer entry with a 270-day national-consultation window, making Qatar the second GCC member to formalize and pushing the perimeter to fifteen named candidates plus the originating UK and EU. The OECD GENAI attestation field schema, finalized Friday, is now circulating among member states on schedule for the June 2-6 plenary, with the secretariat noting the schema's fifteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field coverage now exceeds the originating bilateral memoranda's scope.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS — fifth session inside the second-week base
items.diff_narrative: Friday printed a fourth consecutive consolidation day closing the second trading week at $198.60. Saturday is a sell-side weekend-coverage cycle with no fresh tape: Bernstein's week-recap note reaffirms the structural-second-week-base characterization and holds the $185 Market-Perform floor, Morgan Stanley keeps the $192 target with the upside-scenario probability still at 41 percent, and the five-desk spread holds its roughly $185-to-$235 band. Institutional-buyside net position holds near 37 percent of float and trailing-five-session turnover holds above $6.1B — the Friday figures carried forward rather than re-rated.

items.headline: Mag-7 print-cycle preview — Alphabet analyst day at T-minus-five
items.diff_narrative: The May 21 Alphabet analyst day steps from Friday's T-minus-six to T-minus-five calendar days. The six-desk preview cohort holds the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability at 87 percent (unchanged from Friday's lift), now treating the four-consecutive-day Cerebras consolidation and the Friday Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter as settled pricing-event inputs rather than fresh additions. On the AI-accelerator IPO track, Tenstorrent's Corp Fin first-round comment-letter substantive response — filed Friday at the 11-business-day mark — advances toward the formal review-window midpoint, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster holds at six with the confidential-submission target firmed to the final week of June.

items.headline: n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare) exposure taper — day sixteen
items.diff_narrative: The day-fifteen scan rolls to day-sixteen with the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline now at T-minus-five business days. Internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances continue the taper from roughly 2,510 to 2,180, the residual unpatched long-tail share eases from 18 percent to 16 percent, and Censys honeypot exploitation attempts moderate further from 1.9x to 1.6x baseline on the scheduled weekend taper. The CISA federal-civilian operational directive incorporating the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits taxonomy, which cleared the OMB publication queue Friday, remains scheduled for publication early the following week.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry — weekend hold above 90 percent
items.diff_narrative: Friday crossed cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane visibility above the 90 percent threshold to 91 percent. Saturday holds that line with no fresh disclosure over the business-quiet weekend. The median MCP-server-provisioning-to-first-credential-extraction time on unprotected estates holds at 5 minutes for a fifth consecutive day; the unprotected-versus-protected gap moves from Friday's 65x to roughly 67x as protected detection latency extends, and Defender-for-Cloud quarantine on net-new MCP servers ticks from 45 percent to 46 percent — a sixth consecutive day of expansion. The four-orchestrator managed-visibility composition holds at roughly 91 percent of new provisioning events.

items.headline: Agentic-AI loader-verification line — eleven-CVE taxonomy consolidates
items.diff_narrative: Friday added the eleventh CVE (Haystack nested-dependency-resolver path traversal) and a Trail of Bits taxonomy extension. Saturday brings no fresh disclosure; instead the line settles. Trail of Bits publishes a weekend bug-class consolidation write-up reorganizing the eleven-CVE taxonomy into a single four-tier-and-sub-tier reference, and DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a supplementary note to their joint preprint adding a consolidated Python-and-Rust reference-implementation index covering all eleven CVE-pattern instances. The framework maintainer cohort reaffirms the coordinated mid-June default-shipment commitment now covers all five mitigation surfaces.

items.headline: Claude Code 3.0 registry telemetry — day nine, 64 gated tenants held
items.diff_narrative: Day eight rolls to day nine with the second-week growth normalization continuing — published skills rise from 26,180 to roughly 27,640 (+5.6 percent, a third consecutive sub-7-percent reading) and auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills go from 58 to 62. Unlike Friday, which added Leonardo, Hensoldt, Kongsberg, and Patria to push the Mythos-Preview gated cohort to 64, Saturday reports no weekend signings — the cohort holds at 64. The verification harness's cross-tenant compositional safety check tightens further from under 58 seconds to under 55 seconds via additional parallel-verification optimization.

items.headline: Mistral Workflows and OpenAI per-org agent registry — weekend hold
items.diff_narrative: Friday landed Belgium's FOD Financien as Mistral's seventh sovereign-cloud central-government reference and extended OpenAI's Indo-Pacific GA cohort to eight regions. Saturday is a hold-steady weekend for both: Mistral reports no fresh central-government estate selection (the seven-reference cohort unchanged, tenancy edging to roughly 392 customers) and OpenAI reports no fresh regional extension (the eight-region footprint held, GA-cohort tenancy near 341). Both keep the five-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix on its first-week-of-June general-availability target; OpenAI ships Codex CLI v3.1.4 as a Saturday point release consolidating the client-side mitigation surface, succeeding Friday's v3.1.3.

items.headline: Open-source serving stacks — weekend hold before Monday vLLM stable cut
items.diff_narrative: Friday advanced vLLM to v0.11.4-rc2, SGLang RadixArk to v0.5.9, and TGI to v3.2.2, each adding the nested-dependency-resolution mitigation. Saturday is a hold-steady benchmark cycle with no revision bump — the versions carry forward unchanged ahead of the now-imminent Monday May 18 vLLM v0.11.4 stable cut. The Yotta Labs throughput gap holds near 2.7 percent, effectively flat against Friday and still the tightest of the cycle, and Cloudflare Infire holds L40S edge-tier parity at 1.00x.

items.headline: Tenstorrent Galaxy rack shipments — seventh-wave weekend top-up
items.diff_narrative: Friday's seventh-wave cadence lifted cumulative racks from 132 to 153. Saturday adds a small weekend top-up bringing the cumulative count to roughly 162 racks against the 280-rack first-half target, with additions spread across the North American neocloud cohort plus small Asia-Pacific increments; the European and Latin American sovereign-cloud cohorts hold at their Friday counts. AMD's Helios plus MI450 commitment book holds near 10.1GW with no fresh weekend sovereign-cloud commitment, and the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 review window holds its early-August public-filing target.

items.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 — seventh cohort, weekend-shift three-line cadence
items.diff_narrative: Friday hit 72 active units and the first three-line cross-cell coordination demonstration. Saturday activates a seventh cohort of 12 units, lifting the active count to 84 of the 240-unit allocation (35 percent reached), with cycle-time tightening from a 1.04x to a 1.03x human-baseline envelope. The coordination demonstration extends from Friday's first three-line run into a weekend-shift cadence — roughly thirty-two units across the Fremont automotive, sub-assembly, and battery-module lines. Stellantis Detroit (June 8) and Volkswagen Wolfsburg Optimus (June 22) activation dates hold unchanged.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics Atlas — first North American 72-hour milestone
items.diff_narrative: BMW Spartanburg advances from Friday's first North American 48-hour continuous-operation milestone to the first North American 72-hour milestone with zero MTBF-impacting incidents. Volkswagen Wolfsburg's Atlas pilot scales further from 68 to roughly 80 units on the body-shop welding-jig material-handoff task. The humanoid league-table OEM-adopter roster holds at six with no fresh weekend entry — Friday's Honda Indiana entry is not extended — and Hyundai Metaplant's Dangjin cycle-time improvement holds near 5.1 percent for a fifth consecutive within-band day.

items.headline: Consolidated unified loader-and-manifest verification paper
items.diff_narrative: A Saturday arxiv release (2605.07241) folds the eleven-CVE Trail of Bits taxonomy into a single formal-verification framework with compositional safety theorems covering all five mitigation surfaces as a unified loader-and-manifest verification model, consolidating the prior per-surface artifacts published across the May 5-15 disclosure wave. This supersedes the prior two weeks' per-CVE addenda — Simon Willison characterizes it as the loader-verification line's settling point — and replaces the incremental Friday papers (the standalone nested-dependency-resolution paper 2605.07041 and the v4 runtime-verifier addendum) with a single five-surface reference.

items.headline: Fifteen-jurisdiction cyber-eval reciprocity attestation-schema paper
items.diff_narrative: A second Saturday arxiv release (2605.07289) extends Friday's fourteen-jurisdiction reciprocity-attestation companion paper (2605.07089) to the fresh fifteen-jurisdiction Indo-Pacific cohort following Qatar's Saturday formal entry, supplying compositional safety theorems for the fifteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field interop against the now-finalized OECD GENAI attestation field schema. It models the schema's cross-continental coverage and supplies a verification harness for the per-tenant attestation-log audit trail at fifteen-jurisdiction scale, positioned as a research input to the June 2-6 plenary's draft-Recommendation circulation.
